messages:
Kelsey: Quick Q — we're hitting reconnect storms in the mobile SDK streaming client when the app backgrounds and ephemeral tokens expire (~5m). Flow: socket disconnects -> SDK reconnects immediately -> server returns 401 -> SDK retries again, repeat. Anyone seen this pattern or have recommended fixes?

Ryan: Seen this before. Usually a race between the reconnect logic and token refresh. Two common bugs: SDK tries to reconnect with the old token while a refresh is in flight, and multiple concurrent refreshes create thundering. Also mobile background lifecycle kills sockets so you get repeated disconnects.

Anita: For the Swift client we solved it by adding an authProvider closure that is awaited by the connection code so reconnects block until refresh finishes. Example:
```swift
// pseudocode
connection.authProvider = { completion in
  tokenManager.getToken { result in
    completion(result.token)
  }
}
// connection attempts will wait for authProvider
```
Works well with a single in-flight refresh lock.

Mike: On Android we used an OkHttp interceptor pattern: if response is 401, hold new requests, run single refresh routine, then replay queued requests. Sketch:
```kotlin
synchronized(lock) {
  if (!isRefreshing) {
    isRefreshing = true
    token = refreshToken()
    isRefreshing = false
    replayQueued()
  } else {
    queueRequest(req)
  }
}
```
This prevents duplicate refreshes and reconnect storms.

Emma: Also note for browser/webview cases: avoid cookie-based auth for streaming endpoints inside cross-origin frames — SameSite/Lax drops cookies on navigations. Use Authorization header with the ephemeral token or a postMessage bridge from the native layer. For RN WebView, sending the token via injected JS at load time can be simpler than relying on cookies.

Ryan: Operational checklist we use: 1) stop automatic reconnect until token refresh completes, 2) single-refresh lock per client, 3) exponential backoff with jitter after N failed attempts, 4) fallback to polling for a cooldown window if streaming keeps failing, 5) emit a metric for "stream_reconnects_per_minute" to alert.

Kelsey: Good tips — what's the recommended backoff values? We don't want to block UX but also avoid spamming.

Anita: We do immediate retry once after a short jitter (200-500ms) if refresh already completed, then backoff 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s up to 1min. Also cap total retry attempts in a short window (e.g., 6 tries / 5 minutes) then surface an error to the app.

Kelsey: What about background keepalive pings? iOS will often drop sockets after backgrounding. Should SDK keep sending pings?

Mike: Don't rely on background sockets. On iOS treat background as paused: stop reconnect attempts and surface a "paused" state. On Android if you need long-lived streams you must run a foreground service (and request the permission).

Emma: For RN clients: listen to AppState and explicitly call connection.pause() when backgrounded and resume when foregrounded. That avoids immediate reconnect storms when the OS kills the socket.

Kelsey: Cool. I'll implement: (1) authProvider blocking reconnects, (2) single refresh lock + queued replay, (3) backoff cap, (4) pause on background. Will ping for review. Thanks! :raised_hands:
